reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in Chinese food
Located a 2-minute walk from Exit 3 of Jongno 5-ga Station.
Jajangmyeon is 7,000 won, sweet and sour pork (beef) is 22,000 won.

This is Chinese food!
Jjajangmyeon has to be thick to taste good.
It's a bit difficult to rub, but it's still good.
Chunjang (chunjang) must be stir-fried in sizzling oil to make true jjajang!
I was satisfied because it was my favorite style of Jjajangmyeon.
It harmonizes well with pickled radish, so the perfection is high.
The short uni-style meat is a bit disappointing,
The sweet and sour pork that we ordered together fully covers this.
The portion of sweet and sour pork is quite generous and can feed two people!
It would be great to have a mini size for those who eat alone.
The outside is quite crispy and feels like it has a sweet coating.
It seems as if a large fish is shouting, “I am a meat!”
A style where you can feel the harmony of sweet and salty even without dipping it in soy sauce!
It is a sweet and sour pork that looks good and is overall satisfying.
However, since the meat is dry, people with weak teeth like me may feel a bit of pain in the jaw afterwards.
A Chinese restaurant with a similar feel is ‘Gang Dong-won’.
Personally, this one suited my taste better because it was less sweet and had a good sweet-salty balance.
In particular, the sweet and sour pork here is easy to drink, while Kang Dong-won's is a bit sweet, so you get sick of it quickly after eating 3-4 pieces.

Store & Tips & Review
The store is not as small as expected, and there are quite a few tables.
There are also window seats, so it's a good place to eat alone.
Write your name and menu on the waiting board at the entrance and wait~
When I visited at 7:15 on a weekday evening, there were 3 teams in front of me and I had to wait about 15 minutes.
It closed right after I entered, so I recommend visiting around 7 o'clock if you want to go steadily.
It's not a place with a diverse menu like a local Chinese restaurant, but
Due to its composition, it is more suitable for two people rather than eating alone.
It’s growing in popularity these days, so visit in advance!
And kindness is a bonus.

Yeonsinnae’s amazing Algoni Jjambbong restaurant #Dohwarim
Now, as we know, it is the golden age.
Algony is added to the spicy soup.
Nowadays, algoni is even added as a garnish to Jjambbong, the second most popular hangover dish in Korea.

Although it is not that well-known among Chinese restaurants in Eunpyeong-gu, it is a place with great skills.

Egg Jjamppong (9,000) Beef Jjamppong (9,000)
The broth itself is not spicy and rich, but you will be captivated by the subtle spiciness and rich, savory taste of the broth that goes beyond the basics.
In addition, because of the large amount of algoni, you may feel full.

The hidden card, bean sprout yulingi (19,000), combined with the strong acidity of bean sprouts and the crispy, moist yulingi, seems to be very suitable for Kaoliang liquor consumed during the day.

If you want to enjoy a quiet daytime drink, I recommend Dohwarim.

It's a small, simple restaurant, but the food is exceptional. Overall, it is well balanced without being overpowering, and the texture is decent. The price range is also reasonable.

Clam chowder (11,000 won), unlike soups usually sold in Italian restaurants, contained a generous amount of ingredients such as clams, mushrooms, and broccoli, and was good because it was not watery but slightly thick.

The baguette sandwich (11,000 won) is filled with apples, cheese, arugula, butter, and basil pesto inside a crispy baguette that is not too tough. It's a simple combination, but the flavor is good, so it looks like they're using good ingredients.

Ragura Lasagna (20,000 won) had both ragusa sauce and bechamel sauce that were deep without being overpowering. The lasagna noodles were cooked just right.

During dinner hours, the hall is only available for rental, and during lunch hours, it is usually full unless you go early. I'm also curious about the basil pasta and French rack and plan to visit again.

reviews.author: Sean “Ernie” Jeong
reviews.text:
It's a restaurant you want to keep secret and don't want people to know about. The reason is... the food is neat and delicious. You can feel the sincerity and handmade taste. The atmosphere is also good. Especially at dinner, you can enjoy it without worrying about the table next to you. However, the restaurant's identity is ambiguous. Italian... right?
Lasagna named 'Ragu'... delicious. Both the ragu sauce and pasta texture are good.
French(?) rack lamb... I don't know if it's because I like lamb with a meaty flavor, but it seems like it's not enough by 1%... However, people who have an aversion to the meaty flavor of lamb will like it. The doneness of the meat is also good.
Clam chowder... Cream soup with clams... Of course it's delicious. It reminds me of Fisherman's Warf in San Francisco or Boston. However, the scent of clams is a bit disappointing. And the bread was greasy... it would have been better if it was a little lighter...
The Magari plate is nice, with a variety of cheeses and house-baked crackers. The pairing with wine is especially good. It was nice to have creamy goat cheese, but the amount of olives was a bit lacking. But it doesn't matter. I just need to order more...
I was also satisfied with the crispiness of the baguette and the salad. I also liked the highlighting of the seaweed, which requires a lot of work.
For dinner, we only accept rentals for one group (maximum of 16 people, but up to 8 people can enjoy a leisurely meal). You must make a reservation. You can dine in during the day without a reservation.
You can bring wine, but there is a corkage charge of 20,000 won per bottle. However, the wine glass is not changed often. And the evening rental fee is a bit steep at 30,000 won per hour. Therefore, the cost-effectiveness is not good. Go during the day. lol

reviews.text:
One of the best foods I discovered in Korea (maybe even the best): hotteok!
If you are Korean or have been to Korea, if I don't know hotteok, it means I don't know anything... but there is no hotteok in Barcelona. 😔 I really wonder why! 🤔
The first time I tried hotteok was at a cafe in Myeongdong. It was pre-made, and although it was delicious, I wasn't completely in love with it. But on the same day, I tried freshly baked hotteok at Myeongdong Night Market, and it was even more delicious! 🤩
While I was waiting in line to buy hotteok for the second time, I saw a sign that said “cinnamon,” “honey,” “sugar,” and “peanuts.” Since the hotteok I ate in the afternoon was sweet, I thought I should choose the cinnamon flavor. But I didn’t have to choose! Hotteok is made from wheat flour and contains a lot of my favorite ingredients!

I ate hotteok several times during my stay in Seoul, but the best was the hotteok I ate at Hoshi Tam Tam Square. It was really delicious! I argued with my son for a while about having hotteok instead of eye cream... but in the end, he ate almost all of it! 😡
The other stores near the entrance were very crowded, but it was nice that there was no line at Hoshi Tam Tam Square. Honestly, I can't imagine that other stores would taste better 🤔, but now I'm curious... I'll have to go and try it again! 😋
For reference, one hotteok costs 2,000 won, or about 1.3 euros... 😅

You use a whisk to stir the dough in the kettle, and you used the whisk in the sink behind you and threw it. reviews.text:
People who don't eat bread even when it is in front of them.
After grumbling after a bad lunch, my friend who likes bread came in because he wanted to try it at this place he had passed by before.

After meeting the impressive owner and his wife, I thought this place had a nice atmosphere, but since I wanted a cold latte, my companion told me to eat two salt breads and fill up my stomach, and I was planning to eat soup and rice somewhere else.
After taking a bite of salt bread, I immediately asked for pecan pie, raspberry pie, and walnut rye bread that I had requested for breakfast tomorrow, so I packed the leftovers.

Until now, I thought that a store in Seongsu-dong had the best salt bread, but that wasn't the case. The texture is like pastry, with just the right amount of butter and saltiness. The size is also large.
Pecan pie and raspberry pie taste just like eating at a good bakery while traveling abroad. Especially raspberry pie, when you bite into it, you get raspberry jam ➔ a slight hint of cinnamon ➔ 3 consecutive hits of savory nuts. Mu.Rung.Do.Won. It's so delicious that I'm cutting my companion's pie, but hey, stop cutting and quickly make this Hammu Bar.
And walnut rye bread. It's my first time eating rye bread with such a soft texture. At first I thought it was bread. After listening to the boss's explanation, I was convinced. The rye bread itself is savory, but even the walnuts. What is that rye bread with the texture of a delivery box that I used to eat with salad in the morning?

I'm one of those people who eats soup whenever they eat anything, but the taste here makes you forget the price. Plus, a quiet atmosphere + friendly owner couple + clean bathroom.

I found out that the lady boss was from Le Cordon Bleu.

The salt bread was covered with a very thin, crispy crust on the outside, but the inside was soft and moist, and the buttery aroma that spread throughout your mouth was amazing. My companion said that it was the best hwinangsi he had ever eaten since he was born. It was really delicious, but it was a bit crunchy on the outside and had a combination of flavors that I couldn't find anywhere else, so it was really hard to choose. I've tried other breads, but I'm too overwhelmed to write a review so I can't write any more. You can't skip anything with real bread, so eat as much as possible.

I came to see a performance at Doosan Art Center.
I visited.

We prepare side dishes for you to eat together when you order.

It's soft and delicious.

The electric grilled whole chicken is crispy and delicious.
